title: Domain model to PostgreSQL schema
idea: Mapping a domain model to a schema means each entity becomes a table, each field a typed column, and each invariant a key or constraint.

analogy.text: The Java class is a house plan; the schema is the building inspector. Every rule on the plan is checked again on site.
analogy.breaks: An inspector visits once; constraints check every single write.

points: Classes become snake_case tables; fields become columns of the closest exact type.
Money is BIGINT minor units, time is TIMESTAMPTZ, enums are TEXT with CHECK.
References become foreign keys; uniqueness rules become UNIQUE or partial indexes.
Add an index only for a query you can name, and say which.

What it guarantees
rows: table slot, id TEXT PRIMARY KEY

hero.caption: Each row repeats a Java rule in the database, so a bug in one layer cannot corrupt data.

code.title: The Java model
code.caption: Records with invariants in their constructors. The schema below enforces the same rules again.

walk.text: Enum states become a TEXT column with a CHECK listing them.
Ids are String, money is long minor units, times are Instant.
The compact constructor refuses a bad slot before any SQL runs.
`version` is there for optimistic locking on page 5.
One valid slot prints; two invalid ones are refused.

code.title: Schema and constraints
code.caption: The same model as tables on a real PostgreSQL 18, then seven writes. The database refuses the bad ones by itself.

walk.text: `slot`: foreign key to doctor, BIGINT fee, named CHECKs, one slot per start time.
`appointment`: status as TEXT with a CHECK, plus a version column.
Partial unique index: one BOOKED row per slot, while cancelled rows stay.
This index serves one named query: a patient's appointments.
Each attempt prints ok, or the Postgres error code and constraint name.
Double booking, cancel, rebook, bad times, bad fee, unknown doctor, made-up status.
The final rows show the cancelled history and one live booking.

pitfalls: Never store money in a floating type; use BIGINT minor units like `fee_minor`.
Use TIMESTAMPTZ, not TIMESTAMP, so instants stay correct across time zones.
A plain UNIQUE on slot_id blocks rebooking after a cancel; make it partial.

quiz.q: What does schema.mjs print for book after cancel?
quiz.why: The partial index covers only rows WHERE status = 'BOOKED'. After AP-1 is cancelled, no live row holds SL-1, so AP-2 inserts.

takeaway: Every invariant in the Java model needs a matching database constraint.

starters: When should a Java enum be a PostgreSQL enum type instead of TEXT with CHECK?
Should ids be TEXT, BIGINT identity or UUID?
